exposure: liver disease (cholestatic jaundice, viral hepatitis, HELLP syndrome)
outcome: maternal complications (abortion, PROM, preterm labour, IUGR, meconium staining, PPH, ARF, DIC, maternal deaths)
perinatal complications (neonatal hypoglycemia, neonatal hepatitis, neonatal death)
cohort: 65 pregnant women with pre-existing liver disease or suspected liver dysfunction were enrolled.
finding: Liver disease in pregnancy, even if rare in this study, is linked to maternal and perinatal mortality.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery varied among women with different liver diseases, with normal vaginal delivery being the most common across all three categories (cholestatic jaundice, viral hepatitis, HELLP syndrome).
